DENIAL MANAGEMENT

Why 15-22% of Cardiology Claims Get Denied and How PMEX Fixes Each Root Cause

Cardiology has the most modifier-sensitive claims in outpatient medicine. One wrong modifier on a $4,000 catheterization denies the entire claim. PMEX applies current NCCI edits and payer rules before every submission.

17%

U.S. Cardiology Avg. Denial Rate

< 2.8%

PMEX Cardiology Clients Sustained Denial Rate

48hr

Denial Resubmission Turnaround

PATTERN 01

E/M Billed Same Day as Procedure Without Modifier

Cardiologist performs echocardiogram and also evaluates a new complaint in the same visit. The E/M (99214) requires Modifier 25 to indicate it is significant and separately identifiable from the echo. Without it, payers bundle the E/M into the procedure payment and deny the E/M entirely.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews every same-day E/M plus procedure combination and applies Modifier 25 on the E/M when clinical documentation supports a separately identifiable medical evaluation. No same-day E/M revenue lost to missing modifier.

PATTERN 02

Separately Billed Procedures That Payers Consider Inclusive

Stress echo billed alongside resting echo on same date, Medicare bundles them. Right and left heart catheterization billed as two separate line items when combined code (93453) applies. These NCCI violations trigger automatic denial and recoupment audit risk.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies current NCCI edits before every cardiology claim. Procedures bundled by CMS or major commercial payers are correctly combined or separately billed with appropriate modifiers (59, XS, XU) where applicable. NCCI table updated continuously.

PATTERN 03

High-Value Procedure Performed Without Active Authorization

Cardiac catheterization (93454), nuclear stress test (78452), or ICD implant (33249) performed without confirmed prior authorization. Payer denies the entire high-value claim, often $3,000 to $15,000 per procedure, and appeals require months to resolve.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX Prior Auth manages pre-authorization for every high-value cardiology procedure with clinical documentation attached. Authorization confirmed before the appointment is scheduled. No cardiology procedure proceeds without active payer approval in place.

PATTERN 04

Global Billed When Practice Only Performs One Component

Hospital-based cardiologist bills global echo (93306) when the practice only performed the professional interpretation component, the technical component belongs to the facility. Payer denies the technical component because the facility billed it separately. Revenue lost and compliance risk created.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies Modifier 26 (professional component) or TC (technical component) based on your practice's facility relationship for every cardiology diagnostic procedure. Split billing is managed correctly for hospital outpatient, ASC, and independent diagnostic settings.

PATTERN 05

Remote Cardiac Monitoring Billed Without Minimum Day Threshold

Remote cardiac monitoring (99454) requires 16 days of data in a 30-day period. Claim submitted after 12 monitoring days. Medicare and commercial payers auto-deny for insufficient monitoring period, and the recurring monthly revenue stream disappears.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks monitoring day counts per patient per month before submitting RPM claims. 99453, 99454, 99457, and 99458 are submitted only when threshold requirements are met and documented. Recurring monthly cardiac monitoring revenue is never denied for threshold errors.

PATTERN 06

Nuclear Stress Test Denied for Insufficient Clinical Indication

Nuclear stress test (78452) ordered for patient with stable symptoms and no recent change in clinical status. UnitedHealthcare and Aetna require specific documentation of new symptoms, abnormal EKG changes, or risk factor escalation. Claims denied retroactively after imaging is completed.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews cardiology imaging orders against payer-specific medical necessity criteria before prior authorization is submitted. Clinical indication is confirmed in the documentation before the test is performed, never after.

THE EDUCATION

What Is Cardiology Billing And Why NCCI Bundling Changes Everything

Cardiology billing isn't just complex, it's the highest-dollar, highest-scrutiny billing category in outpatient medicine. One modifier error on a single catheterization claim can cost thousands.

Cardiology billing services are the specialized process of coding, submitting, and managing insurance claims for cardiovascular procedures, from routine echocardiograms and stress tests to complex interventional procedures like coronary angioplasty, pacemaker insertion, and cardiac catheterization.

When a patient receives a nuclear stress test, heart ultrasound, or pacemaker implant, billing experts must know exactly how to document it so insurance companies. Like Medicare, United Healthcare, Humana, Tricare, BCBS will pay the cardiologist fairly. What makes cardiology billing exceptionally complex is the layering of procedure codes, add-on codes, modifiers, and medical necessity requirements that govern every single claim.

A simple stress test (CPT 93015) can generate multiple billable components when combined with nuclear imaging, physician interpretation, and technical component billing, each requiring the correct modifier and documentation to avoid bundling denials. The NCCI (National Correct Coding Initiative) bundles many cardiovascular codes that physicians expect to bill separately. Modifier 51 and modifier 25 are among the most commonly miscoded in cardiology. The average cardiology practice loses 12–18% of potential monthly revenue to these errors.

PMEX Cardiology Billing Services connect directly to your existing EHR to capture charges accurately, then apply certified cardiology-specific coding, NCCI compliance, and MIPS optimization, turning your clinical documentation into maximum reimbursement without any EHR migration.

Zero Additional Clinical Burden: Your practice earns every MIPS point it qualifies for without adding data entry work to your physicians or staff.

The Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) is Medicare's performance grading system , and for cardiologists, it's one of the biggest financial levers in the practice. Score below 75 points and Medicare cuts your payment by 9%. Score above 75 and you earn bonus payments.

On $1M in annual Medicare revenue, the swing between a low MIPS score and an optimized one can be $180,000 or more. Most cardiology practices don't have a systematic process for selecting the right quality measures, tracking performance throughout the year, or submitting data to CMS correctly.

PMEX manages the complete MIPS workflow directly from your existing EHR, measure selection, real-time performance tracking, documentation alignment, and CMS submission, so your practice earns every point it qualifies for without any additional reporting burden on your clinical team.

Everything you need to know about PMEX cardiology billing services

No. PMEX integrates directly with your existing EHR, Epic, Cerner, Athena, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, Modernizing Medicine, and 35+ others. Your clinical team keeps using the same system they know. PMEX connects to it, captures charges automatically, and manages all billing downstream. No migration, no retraining, no disruption. Most integrations are live within 3–5 business days.

PMEX manages the full MIPS workflow directly from your existing EHR data, selecting the highest-value quality measures for cardiology (CAD, heart failure, hypertension), tracking performance throughout the year, ensuring documentation meets CMS reporting requirements, and submitting data. Scoring below 75 triggers Medicare cuts; PMEX keeps you above threshold and captures available bonus payments averaging $90K+.

PMEX applies NCCI edits and cardiology-specific bundling logic before every claim submission. When a cardiologist performs multiple procedures in the same session, our coders determine which can be separately billed with modifiers (51, 59, XS) and which are considered inclusive, preventing both undercoding and triggering payer audits. NCCI rules are updated continuously in our scrubbing engine.

Yes. PMEX audits denied cardiology claims, identifies root causes (prior auth issues, modifier errors, bundling violations), and resubmits corrected claims within 48 hours. We also track denial patterns systematically, if the same modifier error is causing repeated denials, we fix it at the source so it stops happening across all future claims.

Yes. PMEX bills remote physiological monitoring for cardiac patients using CPT codes 99453, 99454, 99457, and 99458 plus device-specific codes. We manage the 16-day minimum monitoring threshold tracking and monthly claim generation, capturing recurring revenue from your existing cardiac monitoring program. Most practices we onboard have never billed these codes correctly.

PMEX Prior Auth manages pre-authorization for high-value cardiology procedures, catheterizations, pacemaker implants, EP studies, nuclear imaging, using clinical documentation pulled directly from your existing EHR. We submit with documentation attached, track status in real time, and alert scheduling when authorization is secured. Average approval: 36 hours. Zero scheduling cancellations due to auth gaps.

Yes. PMEX manages split billing for global, professional (modifier 26), and technical (modifier TC) components of diagnostic cardiology procedures, echocardiograms, stress tests, Holter interpretation, based on your practice's specific facility relationship. This is a frequently missed revenue element in cardiology practices that perform both components.

PMEX integrates with Epic, Cerner/Oracle Health, Athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, Modernizing Medicine, Allscripts, Kareo, DrChrono, and 35+ additional EHR platforms. For cardiology-specific systems (Epic Cupid, Cerner CardioAdmin), we support the full charge capture and documentation workflow. Integration setup is typically complete within 3–5 business days.

Yes. All PMEX cardiology billing specialists hold AAPC certification with dedicated cardiology specialty training, not general medical billing. They know cath labs, echo reports, NCCI cardiology-specific bundles, and payer-specific cardiac procedure policies inside out. Cardiology coding is their specific expertise, not a rotation.

PMEX monitors every payment against your payer-specific contract rates and fee schedules. When a payment falls below your contracted rate, we identify the discrepancy, document the contract language, and file a formal appeal with the payer. Systematic underpayments, where a payer is consistently paying below contract for specific cardiology procedures, are escalated for contract renegotiation support.
